subject: Food Science
title: Smoke Flavoring
description: A quick, practical guide to Smoke Flavoring.

hook.text: Most 'smoked' bacon never saw a flame. Liquid smoke—condensed real smoke—does the job in seconds.

buildup.text: Liquid smoke was invented in 1895 by Ernest Wright, who condensed hickory smoke into a bottle.

discovery.text: Real wood smoke contains over 200 flavor compounds. Liquid smoke captures most of them through condensation.

twist.text: Traditional smoking produces polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons—known carcinogens. Liquid smoke has fewer of them.

climax.text: The EU restricted traditional smoke flavoring in 2024 after risk assessment flagged genotoxicity concerns.

punchline.text: The fake version may be safer than the real thing. Irony smoked.

quiz.question: How does liquid smoke compare to traditional smoking in terms of carcinogen content?
options: Liquid smoke has fewer carcinogenic compounds than traditional smoking
